subject: RFP: Data protection evidence — residency, export controls & DPA annex
messages:
From: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@aventra-thera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aventra Therapeutics Legal <legal@aventra-thera.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aventra-thera.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: Data protection questionnaire — residency & export controls

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Aventra is running a security & privacy deep-dive as part of our vendor selection. We appreciate a single consolidated response that covers:

- DPA annex (processor obligations + standard contractual clauses/DPF alignment)
- Evidence of cross-border transfer safeguards (technical + contractual) and any certifications
- Controls for model routing and residence (how requests are routed, where KV cache / inference logs may be stored)
- Subprocessor list and KMS/HSM custody model
- Retention windows for inference request/response logs and auditability for e-discovery
- SLA/backstop options for Dedicated/Private deployments (data residency guarantees)

Can you provide the DPA annex draft plus an evidence pack (control mappings, SOC2 snapshot, and a short matrix showing where data may reside for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments)? We need this to feed our legal and infrastructure teams — target turnaround: 48 hours if possible.

Also flag any items that will require redaction or further legal review on our side.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Regards,
Lucas Martin
Director, Vendor Risk
Aventra Therapeutics

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@aventra-thera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Data protection questionnaire — residency & export controls

Hi Lucas —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a consolidated evidence pack and a draft DPA annex tailored to the RFP items you listed. High-level summary below; full details are in the attached files (stubs listed at bottom).

Quick answers (summary):
- DPA Annex: Draft attached (Redwood_DPA_Annex_AVT_20280214.pdf). Includes standard SCC alignment options and an addendum describing Dedicated/Private deployment scoping.
- Cross-border safeguards: We support SCC/DPF alignment paths; technical safeguards include encrypted transit (TLS1.3), tenant isolation on Dedicated, and per-customer KMS keys for Private deployments. See export-controls-evidence spreadsheet for mapping to legal bases.
- Model routing & residence: Hosted API routes by region and cost tier; KV cache lives in the same region as inference execution for hosted and Dedicated pools. Private deployments run entirely in customer VPC (no Redwood-hosted KV). Short matrix in the sheet.
- Subprocessors & KMS: Current subprocessor registry included (sheet tab). KMS options: Redwood-managed (multi-tenant) or customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private. HSM-backed key storage available for enterprise contracts.
- Retention & logs: Default logs retention 30 days for request/response traces (hosted). Longer retention available via contract; logs can be stored in customer-managed buckets for Private. SOC2 snapshot included.
- SLAs & residency guarantees: Dedicated offers contractually-backed throughput and region pinning; Private deployment provides residency guarantee within customer VPC. We'll call out minimum lead times for on-prem package delivery.

Next steps suggested:
1) Confirm which items you need in the DPA annex vs. a separate attestation (legal preference).
2) Tell us which regions (US/EU/APAC) you need pinned for residency.
3) If you want DocuSign for the annex, flag and we can send.

I've looped in Ben (security) and Kimberly (privacy counsel) for any technical or legal clarifications you need.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments (attached as stubs):
- Redwood_DPA_Annex_AVT_20280214.pdf (DPA annex draft)
- export-controls-evidence-20280214.xlsx (control mapping + subprocessor registry)
- soc2-snapshot-2027Q4.pdf (attestation snapshot)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Data protection questionnaire — residency & export controls

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear pack. A couple of technical clarifications we should provide proactively to reduce back-and-forth: 

- Can we explicitly call out where ephemeral KV caches are flushed and whether any debug dumps are ever persisted outside the execution region? I suggest we add a short paragraph to the evidence sheet that states: "KV cache is ephemeral and scoped to inference lifetime; no debug dumps retained by default; persistent cache only when customer enables long-term caching and then only in customer-specified region."
- For hosted customers who opt for longer retention, we should note that logs can be exported to customer-managed cloud storage (and include example retention SLA options: 90 / 365 days).
- Please confirm the exact HSM providers supported (AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM, and Azure Dedicated HSM) — if we support them, add to the registry.

Kimberly — can you review the DPA annex for any redlines we should pre-emptively offer (e.g., liability caps for export-control-related data egress scenarios, or carve-outs for telemetry aggregated for platform improvement)? If legal wants to avoid preemptive redlines, we can surface them as "items likely to be negotiated."

I'll prepare a short addendum paragraph and push an updated evidence spreadsheet by EOD.

-ben
Ben Carter
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa / Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks for the prompt pack, we received the attachments and started an internal review. A few quick clarifications so we can triage: 

1) For the DPA annex, we'd prefer the SCC alignment path with a short addendum for Dedicated regional pinning. Can you send the annex via DocuSign so legal can start redlines in parallel?
2) On retention: can you confirm whether inference logs (request/response traces) can be retained for 365 days under an enterprise contract and, if so, where they will be stored (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed bucket)? We need this for our e-discovery policy mapping.
3) GDPR export question: if a user in the EU triggers a model that completes on a US-hosted node under fallback, is there an automated routing fallback to EU variants (yes/no) and do you log the jurisdictional change in audit events?

If you can respond to these three points, our legal and infra teams can proceed to a formal scoring. We aim to have a shortlist decision by the end of next week.

Thanks — happy to set a 20-minute call if that's faster.

Best,
Priya Shah
Senior Procurement Manager
Aventra Therapeutics
